title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
summary: A 10-year (FY2016–FY2025 + 9M 2026) forensic audit covering $2,868.0M 9M 2026 FCF, working-capital and $450M accrued-litigation cash-flow distortions, the $533.1M European distributor buyout, tax-rate normalization, and $4.42B in 9M 2026 buybacks.

epigraph.quote: Accounting earnings are an opinion; ten years of unlevered free cash flow and rising invested-capital returns are a fact.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: 6.1 Ten-Year P&L and Free Cash Flow Compounding (FY2016–FY2025 + 9M 2026)

From FY2016 to FY2025, Intuitive grew revenue 3.72x from $2,704.5 million to $10,064.7 million, a 15.7% nine-year CAGR [1, 2]. GAAP operating profit rose 3.11x from $948.5 million to $2,945.5 million (13.4% CAGR). GAAP net income climbed 3.87x from $737.5 million to $2,856.0 million (16.2% CAGR) [1, 2]. Across all ten years, Intuitive posted zero operating losses and zero negative free-cash-flow years, even during the 2020 pandemic and the 2023–2024 $2.18 billion plant buildout [1]. FY2017 GAAP net income ($670.9 million) absorbed one-time U.S. tax reform charges, while Q3 2026 GAAP operating profit ($593 million vs. $1,270 million Non-GAAP) absorbed the $450 million antitrust settlement [1, 4].

web_blocks.caption: Intuitive Surgical 10-Year Audited Financial History & 9M 2026 ($ Millions)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue grew 3.7x from FY2016 to FY2025 with zero loss years; 9M 2026 delivered $2,419.8M GAAP EBIT (absorbing the $450M settlement accrual) and $2,868.0M FCF after CapEx eased to $329.0M.

web_blocks.html: 6.2 Balance Sheet Fortress, Working Capital & Cash Conversion

Intuitive carries one of the cleanest balance sheets in large-cap healthcare [1, 3]. At December 31, 2025, total assets reached $20,458.7 million and total equity stood at $17,941.7 million ($17,824.0 million attributable to ISRG) [1, 3]. It held $9.03 billion in cash and investments against zero debt (0.00 Debt/Equity) [1, 3]. By September 30, 2026, cash and investments stood at $6.80 billion after $2.94 billion in Q3 share buybacks and deals [3, 4]. Meanwhile, 9M 2026 operating cash flow jumped to $3,197.0 million, up from $2,138.0 million in 9M 2025 [3, 4]. Liquidity stays deep, with a 3.33x current ratio and a 2.49x quick ratio.

Footnote forensics reveal important working-capital and acquisition shifts beneath the debt-free balance sheet [1, 3]. First, 9M 2026 operating cash flow ($3,197.0 million) included a +$631.8 million boost from higher accrued liabilities—principally the unpaid $450.0 million antitrust settlement awaiting court approval and future cash payout [3]. That non-cash accrual masked an -$822.0 million cash outflow into inventory and leased-system transfers, pushing balance-sheet inventory up 15.7% to $2,128.2 million alongside $1.37 billion net leased systems in PP&E [1, 3]. Second, the $533.1 million March 2026 Southern Europe distributor buyout lifted goodwill from $370.3 million to $557.8 million and net intangibles from $17.1 million to $196.7 million (9M amortization rose 4.1x to $40.4 million), while adding $75.2 million in sales-type lease receivables (total $328.7 million, low credit losses) [3].
6.3 Stock-Based Compensation, Buybacks & ROIC vs. WACC

A fair audit must also track stock-based pay (SBC), tax normalization, and capital return [1, 3]. SBC totaled $788.2 million in FY2025 and $641.8 million pre-tax in 9M 2026 ($632.0M expensed; $104.1M capitalized) [1, 3]. Lower excess equity-award tax benefits ($103.2 million in 9M 2026 vs. $202.5 million in 9M 2025) lifted the 9M effective tax rate from 11.8% to 18.4% (Q3: 21.5%) [3]. Management deployed $4,419.2 million on buybacks across 9M 2026 ($2.94 billion in Q3 alone, leaving $1.8 billion authorized), cutting shares outstanding from 355.1 million to 346.6 million [3].

Intuitive earns an 18.5% return on invested capital (ROIC), beating an estimated 8.5%–9.5% WACC by 900–1,000 bps even while holding $6.8B–$9.0B of cash. Excluding excess cash, return on core net operating assets tops 35%, showing the strength of its Mexicali and Sunnyvale consumables engine. The GAAP-to-Non-GAAP bridge is also clean. Adjustments cover SBC ($788.2M in FY2025), intangible amortization, and rare legal settlements ($450M in Q3 2026), not recurring 'restructuring' charges [1, 3, 4].

Results for 9M 2026 confirm strong free cash flow ($2,868.0 million on $329.0 million CapEx) alongside real cash-timing caveats [3, 4]. Even after expensing $450 million for the antitrust settlement, 9M GAAP operating profit reached $2,419.8 million (+16.3% YoY; 27.8% margin) [3]. With $6.80 billion in cash and investments remaining after $4.42 billion of buybacks and $518.6 million of net M&A cash outflows, Intuitive easily absorbs the pending $450 million settlement payment [3].

A check of lease accounting and off-balance-sheet items shows zero hidden debt risk [1, 3]. Intuitive places roughly half of new da Vinci units on operating leases. It keeps those robots on its balance sheet inside property, plant, and equipment and depreciates them over their useful lives [1]. That accounting is more conservative than booking upfront sales-type lease gains [1]. Facility lease liabilities are small next to $17.94 billion in equity, while the 3.33x current ratio and 2.49x quick ratio guard against hospital budget downturns [1, 3].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Verdict: Zero Financial Engineering Required
paragraphs: Intuitive's 10-year record—3.7x sales, 114.8% cumulative cash conversion, zero debt, and $2,868.0M 9M 2026 FCF—rests on operating cash rather than leverage [1, 3]. Investors must still adjust 9M 2026 CFO for the unpaid $450M settlement accrual, -$822M inventory/lease-fleet absorption, and higher 18.4%–21.5% tax rates [3].

book_subsections.title: Ten Years of Numbers That Refuse to Lie
paragraphs: When you and I sit down with ten years of audited 10-K filings from 2016 through 2025, we are looking for one thing above all else: does the cash flow confirm the story? In Intuitive Surgical's case, the answer is an emphatic yes. Over nine years from 2016 to 2025, revenue nearly quadrupled from $2.70 billion to $10.06 billion, operating income tripled from $949 million to $2.95 billion, and net income grew from $738 million to $2.86 billion. Not once in that entire decade—not during the 2020 pandemic shutdown, not during the 2022 chip shortage—did Intuitive post an annual loss or burn free cash flow.

Look closely at cash conversion across the decade. From 2016 through 2025, Intuitive generated $18.22 billion in operating cash flow against $15.87 billion in GAAP net income—115 percent conversion. After factory CapEx peaked at $1.11 billion in 2024 and eased to $539.8 million in 2025, nine-month 2026 free cash flow hit $2.87 billion on just $329 million of CapEx. Forensic readers must note one timing nuance: 9M 2026 operating cash flow ($3.20 billion) received a temporary lift from the unpaid $450 million antitrust settlement accrual, which offset an $822 million inventory and lease-fleet cash absorption.

book_subsections.title: The Cleanest Balance Sheet in Medtech—And One Honest Caveat on SBC
paragraphs: Walk through the September 2026 balance sheet and you still see zero financial debt alongside $6.80 billion in cash and investments—even after $4.42 billion in nine-month share buybacks and $518.6 million in net acquisition outflows. That $533.1 million March 2026 buyout of Southern European distributors ab medica, Abex, and Excelencia Robótica lifted goodwill to $557.8 million and net intangibles to $196.7 million. Meanwhile, lower employee stock-option tax windfalls pushed the nine-month effective tax rate from 11.8 percent to 18.4 percent.

Stock-based compensation also warrants honest accounting. Intuitive recorded $788.2 million in SBC in 2025 and $641.8 million pre-tax across 9M 2026. Unlike serial diluters, Intuitive retired shares aggressively—cutting common shares outstanding from 355.1 million at year-end 2025 to 346.6 million by September 2026 with $1.8 billion still left on its repurchase authorization.

Finally, check downside protection. With a 3.33x current ratio, zero debt, and $2.87 billion of nine-month free cash flow, Intuitive can pay the $450 million antitrust settlement out of pocket without touching credit lines. Its balance sheet passes our price-blind forensic audit cleanly, provided investors normalize 2026 cash flow for inventory builds and the pending legal payout.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Price-Blind Quality Must Come First
book_callouts.text: Before we ever look at a stock quote or a valuation multiple, you and I have established the fundamental truth about Intuitive Surgical: a debt-free, 84-percent-recurring medical monopoly earning 18.5 percent ROIC with 115 percent ten-year cash conversion. Whether that business is an attractive investment depends entirely on the price we pay—which is what we turn to next.

Walk through the ten-year income statement and cash conversion audit calmly. Over the full FY2016 through FY2025 span, revenue compounded at 15.7% annually from $2,704.5 million to $10,064.7 million, while GAAP operating profit compounded at 13.4% and net income compounded at 16.2%. That widening between operating profit growth and net income growth came from rising interest income on Intuitive's multi-billion-dollar cash pile alongside favorable tax deductions on employee equity awards.

Turning to balance-sheet cash flow quality in 9M 2026, operating cash flow was strong, yet free cash flow cannot simply be multiplied out linearly without adjusting for two hidden drains. First, $329.0 million of 9M 2026 property, plant, and equipment expenditures reflects ongoing da Vinci 5 manufacturing scale-up alongside $533.1 million spent acquiring European direct distribution operations. Second, lease-heavy placements tie up hardware capital inside property and equipment over multi-year operating lease terms before recurring instrument utilization harvests full lifetime cash margin.

This distinction matters enormously for equity underwriting at $399.05 per share. When analysts add back stock-based compensation without deducting the economic dilution cost, they overstate owner earnings by roughly 30%. On an ex-SBC owner earnings basis, true recurring cash yield at nearly 48x trailing earnings drops well below the 5.04% risk-free ten-year Treasury benchmark, forcing strict valuation discipline.
